The Locator indicates where in a Warehouse a product is located.
The preferred Locators are used in inventory moves and receipts based on Priority of the Locator
Identifies an item which is either purchased or sold in this organization.
Maximum capacity of the locator in stocking unit of measure
Minimum stocking quantity of locator in stocking unit of measure

Picking Sequence Number can be defined for zones and locators in the warehouse.
The Picking Sequence in the locator setup, represents the Picking Sequence Number of the locator in the warehouse. Warehouse tasks in a pick list will be sorted by the picking sequence number of the locator. In addition, the rules engine allocates products in the locator picking sequence.
The Picking Sequence in the zone setup represents the Picking Sequence Number of the zone in the warehouse. During product allocation for picking, if a zone is not specified in the rule, the rules engine allocates products in the zone picking sequence of static zones followed by the locator picking sequence.
Picking UOM of locator

The Relative Priority indicates the location to pick from first if an product is stored in more than one location. (100 = highest priority, 0 = lowest). For outgoing shipments, the location is picked with the highest priority where the entire quantity can be shipped from. If there is no location, the location with the highest priority is used. The Priority is ignored for products with Guarantee Date (always the oldest first) or if a speific instance is selected. Incoming receipts are stored at the location with the hoghest priority, if not explicitly selected.

Putaway Sequence Number can be defined for zones and locators in the warehouse.
The Putaway Sequence in the locator setup,represents the Putaway Sequence Number of the locator in the warehouse. Warehouse tasks in a putaway list will be sorted by the putaway sequence number of the locator. In addition, the rules engine will search for locators in the locator putaway sequence.
The Putaway Sequence in the zone setup,represents the Putaway Sequence Number of the zone in the warehouse. When searching for locators to putaway products, if a zone is not specified in the rule, the rules engine searches for locators in the zone putaway sequence of static zones followed by the locator putaway sequence.
Stocking UOM of locator

If defined, the process runs only of the IP address of the computer matches the IP address defined. Example: You defined 10.10.10 - it will run on all IP addresses, which have this as part of the computer address - including 99.10.10.10 or 10.10.10.99

If selected, the process is run only within the tolerance of the specified time - i.e. if it should run Wednesday at 14:00 and the tolerance minutes is 30, the process will not be run if the application server is not available from 14:00 to 14:30.
The toleance in Minutes if the process can run only at the specified time.

The scheduler targets to start the process at the targeted hour/minute and the interval after that. The target hour is in 24 hour (17:00 is 5 PM) of the local system time. Example: Target Hour: 02 - Minute: 00 - Interval: Hour Frequency: 7 The target start date of the scheduler would be 02:00, 09:00, 16:00, 23:00 and then next dat at 02:00 ... If the target hour and minute is 0, this is ignored and only the interval is used to determine the next run.
Minute from 0 to 59 of the process to start

Column.ColumnHelp: A zone is a group of locators within the warehouse
The name of an entity (record) is used as an default search option in addition to the search key. The name is up to 100 characters in length.

Picking Sequence Number can be defined for zones and locators in the warehouse.
The Picking Sequence in the locator setup, represents the Picking Sequence Number of the locator in the warehouse. Warehouse tasks in a pick list will be sorted by the picking sequence number of the locator. In addition, the rules engine allocates products in the locator picking sequence.
The Picking Sequence in the zone setup represents the Picking Sequence Number of the zone in the warehouse. During product allocation for picking, if a zone is not specified in the rule, the rules engine allocates products in the zone picking sequence of static zones followed by the locator picking sequence.

Putaway Sequence Number can be defined for zones and locators in the warehouse.
The Putaway Sequence in the locator setup,represents the Putaway Sequence Number of the locator in the warehouse. Warehouse tasks in a putaway list will be sorted by the putaway sequence number of the locator. In addition, the rules engine will search for locators in the locator putaway sequence.
The Putaway Sequence in the zone setup,represents the Putaway Sequence Number of the zone in the warehouse. When searching for locators to putaway products, if a zone is not specified in the rule, the rules engine searches for locators in the zone putaway sequence of static zones followed by the locator putaway sequence.

Replenishment Sequence Number of the “destination” zone in the warehouse. When searching for locators to replenish products, if a zone that is to be replenished (destination zone) is not specified in the generate replenishment process, the system replenishes locators in the zone replenishment sequence of static zones followed by the locator putaway sequence.

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

Example: "Updated-Created" would list the age of the entry in days

The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.
A description is limited to 255 characters.

The display length is mainly for String fields. The length has no impact, if the data type of the field is - Integer, Number, Amount (length determined by the system) - YesNo (Checkbox) - List, Table, TableDir (length of combo boxes are determined by their content at runtime)

format := {expression} [{logic} {expression}]
expression := @{context}@{operand}{value} or @{context}@{operand}{value}
logic := {|}|{&}
context := any global or window context
value := strings or numbers
logic operators := AND or OR with the previous result from left to right
operand := eq{=}, gt{>}, le{<}, not{~^!}
Examples:
@AD_Table_ID@=14 | @Language@!GERGER
@PriceLimit@>10 | @PriceList@>@PriceActual@
@Name@>J
Strings may be in single quotes (optional)
The Length indicates the length of data in a column as defined in the database.

format := {expression} [{logic} {expression}]

Picking Sequence Number can be defined for zones and locators in the warehouse.
The Picking Sequence in the locator setup, represents the Picking Sequence Number of the locator in the warehouse. Warehouse tasks in a pick list will be sorted by the picking sequence number of the locator. In addition, the rules engine allocates products in the locator picking sequence.
The Picking Sequence in the zone setup represents the Picking Sequence Number of the zone in the warehouse. During product allocation for picking, if a zone is not specified in the rule, the rules engine allocates products in the zone picking sequence of static zones followed by the locator picking sequence.
The Processed checkbox indicates that a document has been processed.

Putaway Sequence Number can be defined for zones and locators in the warehouse.
The Putaway Sequence in the locator setup,represents the Putaway Sequence Number of the locator in the warehouse. Warehouse tasks in a putaway list will be sorted by the putaway sequence number of the locator. In addition, the rules engine will search for locators in the locator putaway sequence.
The Putaway Sequence in the zone setup,represents the Putaway Sequence Number of the zone in the warehouse. When searching for locators to putaway products, if a zone is not specified in the rule, the rules engine searches for locators in the zone putaway sequence of static zones followed by the locator putaway sequence.
When a Warehouse Task is prepared, the requisite quantity from the source locator is "dedicated" to the task, and cannot be used for any other purpose.
The Quantity Entered is converted to base product UOM quantity.
Quantity suggested for Pick or Putaway by the Putaway or Pick process
The SKU indicates a user defined stock keeping unit. It may be used for an additional bar code symbols or your own schema.

For the Cluster Pick method, when the wave is released, the system generates a unique Slot No for each Sales Order in the Pick List. The Slot Number is printed on the Pick List, and the operator must place the picked products in the Slot Number indicated.

Under some circumstances, the operator may need to split a task. For example, in the case of a putaway task, if the targeted quantity does not entirely fit into the suggested destination locator, the operator may decide to putaway some quantity in a different locator. In this case, the task can be split into two tasks by clicking on the ?Split task? button.

ValidationRule.ValidationCode: C_Period.IsActive='Y' AND PeriodType='S' AND C_Period.C_Year_ID IN (SELECT C_Year_ID FROM C_Year INNER JOIN MRP_Plan ON (MRP_Plan.C_Calendar_ID = C_Year.C_Calendar_ID) AND (MRP_Plan.MRP_Plan_ID = @MRP_Plan_ID@)) AND (C_Period.C_Period_ID NOT IN ( SELECT MRP_ForecastLine.C_Period_ID FROM MRP_ForecastLine WHERE (@MRP_Forecast_ID@ = MRP_ForecastLine.MRP_Forecast_ID ) AND ( MRP_ForecastLine.M_Product_ID = @M_Product_ID@ ) ) ) AND (C_Period.C_Year_ID * 1000) + C_Period.PeriodNo BETWEEN (SELECT (per1.C_Year_ID * 1000) + per1.PeriodNo FROM C_Period per1 WHERE ('@IsPreviouslyFrozen@'='N' AND per1.C_Period_ID = (SELECT MRP_Plan.C_Period_From_ID FROM MRP_Plan WHERE MRP_Plan_ID = @MRP_Plan_ID@)) OR ('@IsPreviouslyFrozen@'='Y' AND per1.C_Period_ID = ( (SELECT CASE WHEN ((per4.C_Year_ID * 1000) + per4.PeriodNo ) > ((per5.C_Year_ID*1000) + per5.PeriodNo ) THEN (per4.C_Period_ID) ELSE (per5.C_Period_ID ) END FROM C_Period per4, C_Period per5 WHERE per4.C_Period_ID = COALESCE ( (SELECT per3.C_Period_ID FROM C_Period per3 WHERE per3.IsActive = 'Y' AND per3.C_Year_ID IN (SELECT C_Year_ID FROM C_Year INNER JOIN MRP_Plan ON ( C_Year.C_Calendar_ID = MRP_Plan.C_Calendar_ID ) WHERE MRP_Plan.MRP_Plan_ID = @MRP_Plan_ID@ ) AND TRUNC(SYSDATE, 'DD') BETWEEN TRUNC(per3.StartDate, 'DD') AND TRUNC(per3.EndDate, 'DD') ) , (SELECT MRP_Plan.C_Period_From_ID FROM MRP_Plan WHERE MRP_Plan_ID = @MRP_Plan_ID@ )) AND per5.C_Period_ID = (SELECT MRP_Plan.C_Period_From_ID FROM MRP_Plan WHERE MRP_Plan_ID = @MRP_Plan_ID@ )))) ) AND (SELECT (per2.C_Year_ID * 1000) + per2.PeriodNo FROM C_Period per2 WHERE per2.IsActive='Y' AND per2.C_Period_ID = (SELECT MRP_Plan.C_Period_To_ID FROM MRP_Plan WHERE MRP_Plan_ID = @MRP_Plan_ID@))

The Mail Template indicates the mail template for return messages. Mail text can include variables. The priority of parsing is User/Contact, Account and then the underlying business object (like Request, Dunning, Workflow object).

There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reports. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for audit purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Account, if there are invoices for this Account record existing. You de-activate the Account and prevent that this record is used for future entries.

Credit Management is inactive if Credit Status is No Credit Check, Credit Stop or if the Credit Limit is 0. If active, the status is set automatically set to Credit Hold, if the Total Open Balance is higher then the Credit Limit. It is set to Credit Watch, if above 90% of the Credit Limit and Credit OK otherwise.

The Credit Limit indicates the total amount allowed 'on account' in primary accounting currency. If the Credit Limit is 0, no check is performed. Credit Management is based on the Total Open Amount, which includes Vendor activities.

The Credit Used indicates the total amount of open or unpaid invoices in primary accounting currency for the Business Partner. Credit Management is based on the Total Open Amount, which includes Vendor activities.

Credit Management is inactive if Credit Status is No Credit Check, Credit Stop or if the Credit Limit is 0. If active, the status is set automatically set to Credit Hold, if the Total Open Balance is higher then the Credit Limit. It is set to Credit Watch, if above 90% of the Credit Limit and Credit OK otherwise.

The Credit Limit indicates the total amount allowed 'on account' in primary accounting currency. If the Credit Limit is 0, no check is performed. Credit Management is based on the Total Open Amount, which includes Vendor activities.

The Credit Used indicates the total amount of open or unpaid invoices in primary accounting currency for the Business Partner. Credit Management is based on the Total Open Amount, which includes Vendor activities.

Valid options are Per Item and Per Batch. With Per Item, the quantity consumed or charged increases in proportion to the number of products being manufactured. With Per Batch, the quantity is consumed once per batch of the product being manufactured. Batch size is specified in the Product window.

Batch size is typically used in costing calculations and manufacturing transactions. You can define costs to be charged per batch of a product being manufactured by using basis type Per Batch. The number of items in a batch is determined by batch size.

Indicates the document types and accounts to be used for a production order.

The Work Order Close Expense Account identifies the account used to record the difference between the value of material, resources, etc. assigned to a work order and the value of the resources, material, etc. consumed in completed assemblies in that work order.
The Production Order Material Overhead Variance Account identifies the account used to track any residual material overhead value in the production order when it is completed.

The Production Order Material Variance Account identifies the account used to track any residual material value in the production order when it is completed.

The Production Order Resource Variance Account identifies the account used to track any residual resource value in the production order when it is completed.
The Production Order Resource Account identifies the account used to record the value of resources assigned to a production order.
The Production Order Scrap Account identifies the account used to track any value associated with scrapped material.
